# Sirach Chapter 33 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 33 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_033_page_001.jpg

---

33:1 No evil will befall the man who fears the Lord, but in trial he will be rescued again and again.

33:2 A wise man will not hate the law, but the one who is hypocritical about it is like a boat in a storm.

33:3 A sensible man will trust in the law, and the law is faithful to him as when inquiring by Urim.

33:4 Prepare your speech and so you will be heard, and bind together your instruction and then answer.

33:5 The heart of a fool is like a cartwheel, and his thoughts are like a rolling axle.

33:6 A stallion horse is like a mocking friend; under everyone who sits upon him he neighs.

33:7 Why does one day excel another, when all the light of every day in the year is from the sun?

33:8 By the Lord's decision they were distinguished, and he made the seasons and feasts different.

33:9 Some of them he exalted and sanctified, and some of them he made ordinary days.

33:10 All human beings are from the ground, and Adam was created from the earth.

33:11 In the abundance of his knowledge the Lord distinguished them, and made their ways different.

33:12 Some of them he blessed and exalted, and some of them he sanctified and brought near to himself; some of them he cursed and humbled, and turned them out of their place.

33:13 Like clay in the hand of the potter — for all his ways are as he pleases — so human beings are in the hand of him who made them, to give them as he decides.

33:14 Good is the opposite of evil, and life the opposite of death; so the sinner is the opposite of the godly.

33:15 Look at all the works of the Most High: they come in pairs, one the opposite of the other.

33:16 I myself was the last to keep watch, like one who gleans after the grape-gatherers; by the blessing of the Lord I got ahead, and like a grape-gatherer I filled my wine press.

33:17 Consider that I have not labored for myself alone, but for all who seek instruction.

33:18 Hear me, you leaders of the congregation, and you rulers of the assembly, give ear.

33:19 To son and wife, to brother and friend, give no power over yourself during your lifetime, and give not your goods to another, lest you repent and must ask for them back.

33:20 While you are still alive and have breath in you, do not let any person exchange your standing.

33:21 For better is it that your children should entreat you, than that you should look to the hands of your sons.

33:22 In all your works keep the upper hand; bring no blot upon your glory.

33:23 At the day when your life reaches its end, at the time of death, distribute your inheritance.

33:24 Fodder and a rod and burdens for a donkey; bread and discipline and work for a servant.

33:25 Set your servant to work and you will find rest; leave his hands idle and he will seek liberty.

33:26 A yoke and a strap will bend the neck; for a wicked servant there are racks and tortures.

33:27 Put him to work, so that he may not be idle; for idleness teaches much mischief.

33:28 Set him to work, for that is what is fitting for him; but if he does not obey, make his fetters heavy.

33:29 Yet do not be excessive with any person, and do nothing without judgment.

33:30 If you have a servant, treat him as a brother, for as your own soul you have need of him.

33:31 If you treat him badly and he goes away and runs off, in which way will you seek him?

33:32 I am joking with you and speaking from experience: when you try to find a runaway, in the way of the upright, you will find him.

33:33 Now my soul takes pleasure in wisdom's teaching, and I am not put to shame in speaking.
